lede: Mountain Village Council meets Wednesday with a genuinely consequential item on the table: a resolution setting a sale price appreciation cap that determines whether deed-restricted units actually stay affordable over time — the kind of mechanics that quietly shape this valley's housing future. Telluride's HARC has a full evening session with the Shandoka Lot redevelopment up for preliminary large-scale review, and the Ouray County Planning Commission holds three public hearings including a repeal of an entire section of their land use code. The week rounds out with the school district's employee housing proposal getting its first formal look at Telluride P&Z.
